newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian jobless rate to worsen - Opp'n.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian jobless rate to worsen - Opp'n.

text.p: Australia's jobless rate would worsen under the new conservative government, fuelled by massive government spending cuts, Opposition leader Kim Beazley said on Thursday.
As new data showed a sharp rise in unemployment, Beazley told Sydney radio 2UE the Liberal-National government's funding cuts in key areas would force more people out of work.

"You can't be sacking the numbers of people that they've (the government) been sacking without having an impact, you can't be cutting back the assistance to industry without having an impact, and you can't knock over those labour market programmes," the Labor leader said.
"Yes, you do have an impact on unemployment. It certainly will get worse."
The outlook was particularly grim for the long term unemployed, Beazley said.
Australia's jobless rate rose to 8.8 percent in August, seasonally-adjusted, from 8.5 percent in July, Australian Bureau of Statistics figures showed.
But Prime Minister John Howard told parliament the former Labor government was "overwhelmingly" responsible for the high unemployment rate.
Howard's government, which won power in March, slashed government spending by A$3.9 billion in the 1996/97 budget announced last month.
